question: What does the medical certificate for EI sickness benefits need to say?
generated_answer:
You must provide a medical certificate that says you are unable to work for each week you are claiming EI sickness benefits. You may be asked to provide a medical certificate even if you are sick for less than 14 days. Service Canada may contact your doctor to obtain additional information if needed. If you are claiming benefits for the same medical condition and your doctor confirms that you are still sick, you may not need to provide another medical certificate. Service Canada will contact you if more information is needed. If you do not provide a medical certificate when asked, your claim for EI sickness benefits may be refused. When do I have to start paying back my debt? You have 30 days to repay your EI sickness benefit overpayment. How do I repay my debt? There are two ways to repay your EI sickness benefit overpayment:

Online: You can set up a payment arrangement in My Service Canada Account. By cheque or money order: Send a cheque or money order to the payment address listed in the Repayment of Benefits Overpayment letter you received. You must write your Social Insurance Number (SIN) on the front of the cheque or money order. If you are unable to repay the full amount of your overpayment, you should contact the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) as soon as possible. The CRA can work with you to set up a payment arrangement. Note: You are responsible for repaying the full amount of your EI sickness benefit overpayment, even if Service Canada is withholding the full amount of your payment. If you are still receiving EI benefits, repaying your overpayment will not affect your EI payments. If you have any questions about your EI sickness benefit overpayment, please call Service Canada at 1-800-277-9914 (TTY: 1-800-529-3742) and ask to speak with an agent about repayment of benefits. Important information

If you do not repay your debt, your debt will be sent to the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for collection. The CRA has strong collection powers that could result in the following:

You may not be able to receive any more EI benefits until you repay your EI sickness benefit overpayment. The CRA may withhold any future federal or provincial government payments you may receive, such as: Old Age Security (OAS), Canada Pension Plan (CPP), or Quebec Pension Plan (QPP) benefits. The CRA may also withhold any tax refunds you may be entitled to. The CRA may also take legal action against you, including garnishing your wages or placing a lien on your property. The CRA may also charge you penalties and interest on your debt. If you have any questions about your debt, please contact the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) at 1-866-424-1300. If you have any questions about your EI benefits, please contact Service Canada at 1-800-277-9914 (TTY: 1-800-529-3742).
